feature: Package the hello mocker as a container image
goalOneSentence: Author Dockerfile, .dockerignore and BUILD.md so the seeded Hello mocker builds into an image that serves /hello on container port 8080, proven by a live docker build + run + curl.
nonGoals: changing the mocker YAML or C#

tasks.title: Author Dockerfile + .dockerignore + BUILD.md for the Hello mocker
tasks.description: The working directory contains Hello/ — a complete, working QaaS mocker project (Hello.csproj referencing QaaS.Mocker + QaaS.Common.Processors Version="*"; one-line Program.cs 'QaaS.Mocker.Bootstrap.New(args).Run();'; hello.mocker.yaml serving GET /hello -> 200 'hello' on Port 8080). Do NOT modify anything under Hello/. Create at the working-directory ROOT: (1) Dockerfile — multi-stage: stage 1 'FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build', WORKDIR /src, COPY . ., RUN dotnet restore Hello/Hello.csproj, RUN dotnet publish Hello/Hello.csproj -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore; stage 2 'FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0' (CRITICAL: aspnet, NOT runtime — the mocker hosts an HTTP server and the runtime image fails at startup, fact base s13 row 7), WORKDIR /app, COPY --from=build /app/publish ., ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "Hello.dll", "hello.mocker.yaml"] (exec-form JSON array; the yaml argument is the mocker config — it was copied to output because the csproj marks it CopyToOutputDirectory Always). (2) .dockerignore with at least bin/, obj/, *.md. (3) BUILD.md documenting exactly: build command 'docker build -t qaas-hello-mocker .', run command 'docker run -d --name hello-mocker -p 8094:8080 qaas-hello-mocker', smoke check 'curl http://127.0.0.1:8094/hello' expecting body 'hello', cleanup 'docker rm -f hello-mocker', plus one sentence on why the final base image must be aspnet:10.0 citing s13#7. The verify gate runs the real docker build and a live curl through host port 8094.
acceptanceCriteria: docker build succeeds from the working-directory root
Container runs detached and answers 'hello' on mapped host port 8094
Final stage uses mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 and BUILD.md cites s13#7

verify.cmd: docker rm -f qaas-eval-e01 2>$null; docker run -d --name qaas-eval-e01 -p 8094:8080 qaas-eval-e01; $body=''; foreach($i in 1..30){ try { $body = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://127.0.0.1:8094/hello -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 2).Content; break } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 } }; docker rm -f qaas-eval-e01 | Out-Null; if($body -eq 'hello'){ Write-Output 'CURL_OK hello'; exit 0 } else { Write-Output "CURL_FAIL body=$body"; exit 1 }

rubric: Dockerfile is multi-stage with publish output only in the final image
ENTRYPOINT exec-form passes the yaml config argument
BUILD.md commands are copy-pasteable and correct
failureModes: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:10.0 in the final stage (s13#7 — boots then dies)
ENTRYPOINT missing the hello.mocker.yaml argument (mocker has no config to load)
COPY of project subfolder paths that do not match the build context layout

portContract: This sprint's mocker(s) MUST listen on HTTP port 8094. Every runner Transaction MUST target http://127.0.0.1:8094 (set the mocker server Port: 8094 and the runner BaseAddress/Port to 8094). Do NOT use the 8080 default from Fact Base examples - use 8094 exactly, or the live end-to-end run cannot connect.
